title: What Does Data Center Operations Do?
summary: Learn how operations teams keep infrastructure observable, safe, and reliable.
objectives: Explain why operations uses procedures, monitoring, maintenance, and documentation.
Sequence the operational lifecycle from observing a system to escalating uncertainty.

vocab.def: A service is available when people can use it as expected.
A planned set of steps for completing work safely.
Transfer a problem to someone with the right authority or expertise.

sections.heading: Operations is a team process
sections.body: Operations teams help maintain availability, reliability, safety, and accurate records. They use agreed procedures so that people can work consistently and communicate clearly.

sections.heading: The operational lifecycle
sections.body: A useful classroom model is MONITOR, DETECT, INVESTIGATE, RESPOND, VERIFY, DOCUMENT, and ESCALATE. The steps can repeat as new evidence appears.

sections.heading: Observe before changing
sections.body: An alert is a reason to investigate, not permission to make an unknown change. In a safe lab, record what you see and ask for help when a step is outside your permission.

practice.prompt: Put these actions in a sensible order: document the result, observe the system, investigate evidence, verify the result, and escalate when needed.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of an operations procedure?
options: To make work safer, repeatable, and easier to communicate
To guarantee that every problem has one cause
To allow anyone to change production systems
quiz.answer: To make work safer, repeatable, and easier to communicate

lab.objective: Sequence a synthetic operations incident and identify where evidence, verification, and escalation belong.

reflectionPrompt: Which operations step would help prevent a small problem from becoming a larger one?
